items.item: Does closing the defect require inventing a new mechanism, or is one already declared in the repository?
items.derivation: Two closing mechanisms are already declared by existing repository files; neither requires new design. (a) Bypass the hook and generate explicitly: Dockerfile.gcp:26 (`npm ci ... --ignore-scripts`) and Dockerfile.gcp:28 (`npx prisma generate`) in its builder, Dockerfile.gcp:51-53 in its production stage; the root Dockerfile already contains the explicit half of that pattern -- Dockerfile:22-23 copies prisma/ and runs `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://localhost npx prisma generate` after the builder install, and Dockerfile:41-42 imports node_modules/.prisma and node_modules/@prisma/client from builder into production-base -- so the postinstall hook (package.json:46) is already redundant for the Prisma client in both stages. (b) Reorder so scripts/ is present before the install: scripts/ is in the build context (.dockerignore:1-20 excludes only .git, .github, node_modules, build, public/build, env/log files and agent dirs) and currently arrives with `COPY . .` at Dockerfile:26, after the install at Dockerfile:20; production-base never receives it (Dockerfile:40-50). Both mechanisms are derived from cited files at base e3f3e4f30e2fc846dc963a12bc74d1fdeddade05 (git diff base..HEAD for Dockerfile, Dockerfile.gcp, package.json and .dockerignore is empty). The isolated positive control recorded in discovery.json finding 1 and runtime-ledger.json (same file set, `--ignore-scripts`, exit 0) confirms the absent lifecycle-script file is the sole cause. No new mechanism is needed.

items.item: Which stages must the fix cover: production-base only, or builder as well?
items.derivation: Both. The declared staging build contract is docker-compose.staging.yml:5-8 (`dockerfile: Dockerfile`, `target: web`); Dockerfile:58 makes web `FROM production-base`, and Dockerfile:41-50 (`COPY --from=builder ...`) makes production-base depend on a completed builder stage, so a build of target web executes the builder install at Dockerfile:20 before the production-base install at Dockerfile:37. Both installs run the same postinstall hook (package.json:46) with scripts/ absent (builder file set Dockerfile:17-18; production-base file set Dockerfile:35). cloudbuild.yaml:43-93 builds the same Dockerfile with targets web, gdpr-worker, search-indexer-worker and domstol-rss-worker (cloudbuild.yaml:10), all `FROM production-base` (Dockerfile:58,64,68,72). Fixing only one stage leaves the declared build failing at the other; the dependency-graph edges Dockerfile:builder:npm-ci -> scripts/postinstall-prisma-generate.mjs and Dockerfile:production-base:npm-ci-omit-dev -> scripts/postinstall-prisma-generate.mjs (both requires-present, both unsatisfied) are the two edges a fix must satisfy.

items.item: Who selects the concrete implementation mechanism (--ignore-scripts plus the existing explicit generation, COPY reordering, or another mechanism satisfying the same contract)?
items.derivation: Already decided by the owner in the frozen design, not an open owner-level decision: docs/architecture/PATTERN-PROOF-ENGINE-01-V1-BOOTSTRAP-RED-ONLY-DESIGN-FROZEN.md:479-481 classifies mechanism selection as writer-lane implementation discretion bounded by closing both RED probes, staying inside the allowed paths, preserving the declared staging build contract and not altering proof policy; lines 486-491 record the owner's correction of an earlier HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED classification; lines 513-528 make the RED probes solution-neutral (they derive the stage state from the candidate, so `--ignore-scripts`, `COPY scripts` reordering or another correct lifecycle change all pass). The gate therefore records the delegation and does not stop before WRITER.

items.item: Does the fix require changing package.json's postinstall hook, scripts/, or any other file outside the Dockerfile?
items.derivation: No. Both mechanisms in item 1 are confined to the root Dockerfile. package.json is structurally excluded from any writer allow-list: packages/mps-pattern-proof/src/validators.ts:158-171 lists `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json` and `.github` among PROOF_POLICY_PATH_PREFIXES that an allow-list may never cover (validators.ts:250-260, error PPE_ALLOWLIST_COVERS_PROOF_POLICY at validators.ts:547-549), and the SCOPE_VIOLATION fixture (BOOTSTRAP design line 541; audit docs/architecture/audits/PATTERN-PROOF-ENGINE-01-V1-BOOTSTRAP-RED-ONLY.md:177) uses exactly a package.json change as its violation example. Removing or altering the hook is also not needed for the declared contract and would change behaviour for consumers that rely on it (.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:52-59 runs `npm ci` on a full checkout where the hook succeeds; the Vercel path does not build any Docker image, deploy-staging.yml:1-7). scripts/postinstall-prisma-generate.mjs:8-17 and scripts/copy-cesium-assets.cjs:4-33 need no change. .dockerignore needs no change (scripts/ already passes, .dockerignore:1-20).

items.item: Is the minimal sufficient change set inside the declared build contract, and does it avoid proof-policy surfaces?
items.derivation: The minimal sufficient change set is {Dockerfile}. The declared contracts reference the file by name and bind to stage names, not to line content: docker-compose.staging.yml:7-8 (`dockerfile: Dockerfile`, `target: web`); cloudbuild.yaml:47-49, 60-62, 73-75, 86-88 (`-f Dockerfile --target=<web|gdpr-worker|search-indexer-worker|domstol-rss-worker>`), with cloudbuild.yaml:10 stating the targets must match. A fix that edits the install steps at Dockerfile:17-20 and Dockerfile:35-37 and keeps the stage names at Dockerfile:16,32,58,64,68,72 leaves both contracts satisfied unchanged, so neither docker-compose.staging.yml nor cloudbuild.yaml needs editing. `Dockerfile` is not in PROOF_POLICY_PATH_PREFIXES (validators.ts:158-171) and matches no PROOF_POLICY_PROBE_PATHS entry (validators.ts:174-189), so an allow-list of ['Dockerfile'] is admissible under validators.ts:539-566; the audit record line 177 and BOOTSTRAP design line 541 use that exact allow-list in the SCOPE_VIOLATION fixture. The concrete allow-list value is fixed by the CandidateArtifact of the later FULL_PATTERN_PROOF unit (BOOTSTRAP design lines 261-280; artifacts.ts:115-131), not by this gate.

items.item: If the writer bypasses the hook with --ignore-scripts, is a separate owner decision needed about the hook's second half (copy-cesium-assets.cjs) not running inside the image?
items.derivation: No decision is required to close the defect. The declared authority is that the staging web build succeeds (docker-compose.staging.yml:5-8), and the RED probes (BOOTSTRAP design lines 497-511) assert only that each stage's install step does not fail for the missing-lifecycle-script reason; neither encodes a requirement to regenerate public/cesium at image-build time. The hook's copy target already exists in the repository: public/cesium/Assets, Widgets, Workers and ThirdParty are tracked git trees at the base (git objects e3f3e4f30e2fc846dc963a12bc74d1fdeddade05:public/cesium/Assets, :public/cesium/Widgets, :public/cesium/Workers, :public/cesium/ThirdParty; unchanged to HEAD), they are not excluded by .dockerignore:1-20 (only public/build is, line 5), and they enter the builder with `COPY . .` at Dockerfile:26 -- which in today's ordering runs after the hook and would overlay its output anyway. production-base never copies public/ (Dockerfile:40-50), so the hook's cesium half has no effect on the runtime image in either stage. The deployed precedent Dockerfile.gcp (lines 1-73) contains no cesium step. A writer choosing COPY reordering instead keeps the hook running. Either way the semantic outcome for the declared contract is identical, so this is writer discretion under item 3, not an owner-level semantic decision.

items.item: Does production-base need the `prisma` CLI (a devDependency omitted by --omit=dev) or a build-time registry fetch to generate the Prisma client?
items.derivation: No. production-base does not generate the client itself: Dockerfile:41-42 copies node_modules/.prisma and node_modules/@prisma/client from builder, and builder installs all dependencies including the `prisma` CLI (Dockerfile:20 has no --omit; package.json:142,169) and runs the explicit generate at Dockerfile:23 with DATABASE_URL set inline (the same dummy-URL device as scripts/postinstall-prisma-generate.mjs:8-10). So a fix that stops the hook from running at Dockerfile:37 removes nothing production-base relies on, and no decision about promoting `prisma` to dependencies or fetching it at build time (as Dockerfile.gcp:51-53 does with `npx prisma generate` after `--omit=dev`) is required for this target.

items.item: Is the authority the fix asserts against resolvable to an already-produced, governed source via an EvidenceLocator, or is any authority missing?
items.derivation: Resolved; no MISSING_AUTHORITY condition. The authority 'the declared staging web build must succeed' is declared directly in docker-compose.staging.yml:5-8 (context ., dockerfile Dockerfile, target web) and resolves through Dockerfile:58 (web FROM production-base) and Dockerfile:41-50 (production-base FROM builder outputs) to the two defective install steps at Dockerfile:20 and Dockerfile:37; cloudbuild.yaml:43-93 is a second declared consumer of the same Dockerfile targets. The npm lifecycle semantics the defect depends on are declared in package.json:46 (the only install-time hook). The frozen design records the same resolution (BOOTSTRAP design lines 187-195) and the state machine resolves the cited file_line locators against the repository (ppe-cli.ts:12-13, RepositoryAuthorityResolver). Every locator above was re-read in this stage at HEAD 21366c531f00e3b5fca4aff00c44025baa8bee72 with git diff base..HEAD empty for each cited file (only the audit record changed between base and HEAD, and its cited lines 206-216 and 313 were re-verified at HEAD).

items.item: Does the change set for this defect extend to Dockerfile.fly, which has the same ordering shape?
items.derivation: No. The owner-nominated target is the root Dockerfile's builder and production-base stages (BOOTSTRAP design lines 99-111 quoting the owner; routine packages/mps-pattern-proof/routine/PATTERN-PROOF-ENGINE-V1.prompt.md:46 `target: { dockerfile: 'Dockerfile', stages: ['builder', 'production-base'] }`), and the RED probes cite docker-compose.staging.yml:6-8 as authority (BOOTSTRAP design lines 501,507). Dockerfile.fly:16-21, 38-45, 63 exhibit the same shape but no compose file or workflow in the repository binds to Dockerfile.fly (discovery.json finding 9; docker-compose.prod.yml:7-10 and .github/workflows/deploy-gcp.yml:89-97 both build Dockerfile.gcp), so no declared authority for this target resolves to it. A change to Dockerfile.fly would fall outside the {Dockerfile} change set of item 5 and would be a SCOPE_VIOLATION for the writer of this target; whether to nominate Dockerfile.fly as a separate target is a future owner nomination, not a decision this fix involves.

items.item: Does applying the fix alter proof policy, verifier authority or the acceptance criteria, and in which run may it be applied?
items.derivation: A Dockerfile-only fix touches no proof-policy surface (validators.ts:158-171) and does not change the RED probes' asserted behaviour or authority evidence (BOOTSTRAP design lines 497-511, solution-neutral per lines 513-528). The sequencing is already declared by the owner and needs no new decision here: BOOTSTRAP_RED_ONLY produces evidence only and applies no Dockerfile fix (BOOTSTRAP design lines 110-111 and 566-574; routine prompt lines 54 and 76; ppe-cli.ts:16 and 52-56, which refuse any other mode), so the engine stops by mode at RED_SYNTHESIS after this gate (state-machine.ts:407-431 advances to RED_SYNTHESIS when every item is MECHANICAL), and the writer candidate belongs to FULL_PATTERN_PROOF, a separate unit with its own go. This stage did not modify Dockerfile, Dockerfile.gcp, Dockerfile.fly, any compose file, package.json, package-lock.json or .github/, and executed no new reproductions (runtime-ledger.json left unchanged).
